description: A registration names the subclass; the code that runs is on the base. Tornado, Django's class-based views, DRF viewsets and Flask's MethodView all share the shape -- the class a route names carries the model and the permissions, and the request handling is written once on a base class in another file -- and the subclass reaches it as `self.something()`, a receiver whose type a frontend without a checker cannot see and a name that is not defined in the file it is written in. Resolving `self.x()` only against the ENCLOSING class left every one of those edges unresolved, and the cost is not a missing edge but a missing SURFACE: measured on jupyterhub, 32 of the 55 functions that read request data and that no enumerated route could reach were inherited handler methods, and the engine reported the route table INCOMPLETE over an enumeration an adjudicator had verified. The routes were there and the calls were there; only the edges between them were not. This corpus asserts NO finding on purpose. What it holds is `parse_body`, which reads the caller's data and which nothing but an inherited-method edge can reach, and a subclass that OVERRIDES that name -- the enclosing class must still win, or the base's body would be attributed to a route that never reaches it. The reachability itself is asserted in core/internal/surface over this corpus's lowered IR, because a finding count cannot express it: a corpus is scored on what it reports, and what changed here is what the engine can SEE. Kept parameterized deliberately -- an injection here would be asserting how an implicit receiver binds its arguments, which is a different defect with its own entry.
